source.stem: What is not a characteristic of all living organisms?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: An ordinary magnifying glass is enough to see the tiniest microorganisms clearly.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: An empty round-bottom flask magnifies the letters just as well as a water-filled flask.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A microscope is required to see a whole adult butterfly.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: A flat windowpane can be used as a magnifying glass.

intelligence.enrichment: The unaided human eye cannot see objects below a certain size; curved glass, a magnifying glass, and microscopes make small things appear larger so they can be observed. Using a suitable magnifying tool -> small objects appear larger -> hidden details become observable. The learner correctly applies this rule: The unaided human eye cannot see objects below a certain size; curved glass, a magnifying glass, and microscopes make small things appear larger so they can be observed. If nothing is visible to my eyes in clear pond water, then there is nothing living there to observe.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Microorganisms: friend and foe. The student must decide: Decide when an object or tiny organism is too small for the unaided eye and must be observed with a magnifying glass or microscope. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key.
